tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Brecht and Epic Theatre

questions.question: Explain the purpose of Brecht's alienation effect and describe three techniques he uses to achieve it.
questions.correctAnswer: V-effect stops emotional identification so the audience analyses the social message. Three techniques: placards (announce content), direct address (break fiction), episodic structure (prevent immersion). Each technique disrupts naturalistic illusion.

questions.question: What is gestus and how does it differ from a naturalistic approach to character?
questions.correctAnswer: Gestus combines gesture with social attitude — it shows the character's social position, not inner psychology. Naturalism explores inner truth; gestus reveals political truth. E.g. a boss's gestus shows power relations, not personality.

questions.question: How would you stage a scene using Brechtian techniques to make the audience think critically about a social issue?
questions.correctAnswer: A practical answer showing: placard before scene, narration, direct address, simple set with exposed equipment, gestus-based performance, song interruption. Each technique linked to the social issue being examined.

questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: name at least four Brechtian techniques; explain the theory behind each; demonstrate practical staging decisions; link each technique to the V-effect; show how the techniques work together to create critical engagement; evaluate their effectiveness. Mark scheme: Brechtian questions test AO1 (practitioner terminology), AO2 (analysing how techniques communicate meaning), and AO3/AO4...
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
